final_message:
Seven of the 33 wells across the eight water systems pass all three screens, spread over Farmer City, Weldon and Waynesville. I pulled them from the Illinois EPA Source Water Assessment Program factsheets on 2026-11-05. The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders were empty, so there was no operations registry to check.

The seven wells that pass, in the order the email ranks them:

| Priority | Water system | Well | Depth | Reported pumpage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Farmer City | WL47648, Well 9 | 188 | 26,478,500 |
| 2 | Farmer City | WL47646, Well 7 | 180 | 21,976,200 |
| 3 | Weldon | WL45047, Well 3 | 167 | 5,500,000 |
| 4 | Weldon | WL45048, Well 4 | 163 | 3,503,040 |
| 5 | Waynesville | WL40006, Well 6 | 162 | 4,319,500 |
| 6 | Farmer City | WL47647, Well 10 | 181 | 0 |
| 7 | Farmer City | WL01130, Well 11 | 192 | 0 |

I recommended Farmer City Wells 9 and 7 as the top options because they have by far the highest reported pumpage. Wells 10 and 11 qualify on paper, but they report zero pumpage, so the email says to confirm actual use first.

Bartlett, Springerton, Enfield, Crossville and Norris City have no qualifying wells. The email gives the reason for each system.

The factsheet page doesn't label units, so I assumed feet for depth and setback and gallons per year for pumpage. Both the workbook and the email state this assumption.

The email is a draft addressed to "[Manager]" and signed "[Your name]". I also saved it as a Word copy. The `.eml` file has the workbook attached, but nothing has been sent. The source URL and retrieval date are in the email and in the workbook.

The Yes/No screening columns in the workbook are typed values, not formulas.

Files are in `outputs/`:
- `Green_H2_Water_Source_Well_Screening.xlsx`
- `Email_to_Manager_Water_Source_Recommendation.eml`
- `Email_to_Manager_Water_Source_Recommendation.docx`

DONE
